AbstractText.Label: INTRODUCTION
AbstractText.content: We sought to determine whether intrabronchial oxygenation would provide adequate gas exchange during both anesthesia induced apneic and cardiopulmonary arrest and cardiac massage (CPR).

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Ten pigs underwent general anesthesia with mechanical ventilation. Blood gases were measured in each animal at 4 min intervals for up to 28 min. An intrabronchial catheter (4 L/min O2) was inserted through an endotracheal tube after respirator cessation. Group A animals (6) were resuscitated with the catheter but without CPR. Group B animals (4) were rendered apneic and cardioplegic and resuscitated by CPR for 28 min using the intrabronchial device.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: All group A animals were resuscitated and survived after 24 min of apnea. Mean pO2 decreased from 378 mmHg (95% confidence interval [CI], 288-468) to 292 mmHg (95% CI, 246-339), P = 0.009; pCO2 increased from 52 mmHg (95% CI, 43-61) to 137 mmHg (95% CI, 116-158), P < 0.0001; and pH decreased from 7.32 (7.29-7.36) to 6.98 (6.92-7.03), P < 0.0001. In a control animal bronchial catheter oxygen flow ceased at baseline and pO2 decreased from 268 to 30 mmHg by 20 min. In group B animals mean pO2 decreased from 426 mmHg (95% CI, 273-579) to 130 mmHg (95% CI, 92-168) after 28 min, P < 0.0001; pCO2 increased from 49 mmHg (95% CI, 41-58) to 73 mmHg (95% CI, 61-86), P = 0.03; and pH decreased from 7.34 (7.33-7.35) to 7.07 (6.98-7.16), P < 0.0001. In the control receiving intratracheal oxygen pO2 decreased from 324 to 88 mmHg after 16 minu of CPR.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Intrabronchial oxygenation provides sustained hyperoxemia during complete apnea and cardiac arrest with CPR.
